prompt: A weather satellite in geostationary orbit appears to hover over the same spot on the equator day after day. What must be true of its orbit?

options.text: It is parked in space with engines holding it still above that spot
It orbits once per day in the same direction as Earth's rotation, at the altitude where that period is possible
It orbits once every 90 minutes, so it is over the spot at the same time daily
It sits beyond the Moon, where Earth looks stationary

explanation: A geostationary satellite orbits over the equator in about 24 hours (one sidereal day), in the same direction Earth spins, at about 35,786 km altitude, so its position relative to the surface stays fixed.
